aim:
The games index: eyebrow, heading, intro, a grid of game cards each linking to its own
page, and a closing CTA. 2 active placements on gamesdesign.co.uk at authoring time.
contract: - Root `section.game-list-section[data-component="game-list"]`.
- `.gl-heading` is unconditional -> must carry text.
- `{{range .items}}` -> at least one `article.gl-card` inside `.gl-grid`. The `{{else}}` arm
renders `.gl-empty` instead, so a placement with no items fails this check by design.
- The `.gl-cta` link is conditional on `{{if .cta_url}}` and is NOT asserted.
- **This fence is STATIC on purpose, and that is a finding, not an omission.** The census
counts this component as interactive because `js_content` is 963 bytes. It is dead twice
over -- see Notes.
proof_note: Single-instance placement; 33 assets probed, all 200. The site's OTHER placement, /games/index.html, 404s `/assets/images/hero.jpg` (the bugs_closed/128 family) and so cannot hold a green baseline.
mutants: 7/7 caught, every check watched red, baseline green
notes: **`game-list`'s JavaScript is dead twice over, measured 2026-08-08.**
1. **It binds nothing that exists.** `js_content` queries `.gl-filter-btn` and
`#gl-load-more-btn`. Neither string occurs in this component's own `html_template`
(grep: 0) nor in either served page (grep: 0). There is no filter bar and no load-more
button to bind to; both loops are no-ops.
2. **It is not delivered anyway.** Neither placement page emits a
`<script src="/tools/assets/game-list.js">` tag -- in fact neither references
`tools/assets` at all -- while the asset itself IS deployed and serves 200 with the real
code in it. The only script either page loads is `/assets/js/snippets.js` (334 bytes),
So there is no client-side behaviour to assert and this contract asserts none. Recorded
rather than filed as a bug: **visitor impact today is zero** -- the component renders
correctly as a static list, and the missing script would add nothing even if it loaded.
What it costs is a false signal in the backlog census (this reads as an interactive
subject needing 30-45 min of JS reading, when it is a 9-minute static one).
**The delivery gap was then measured rather than assumed**: all 38 active placements of
JS-bearing section components were probed against their served pages, and exactly these
TWO (`game-list` on both gamesdesign pages) render the component without loading its
script. Every other placement loads it. So this is a two-page anomaly, not a class.

aim:
A five-question self-assessment: a start screen, five single-choice questions with a
progress bar, and a scored result tier. 2 active placements / 2 sites at authoring time.
contract: - Root `section.ai-readiness-quiz-section[data-component="ai-readiness-quiz"]`.
- `.quiz-headline` is unconditional -> must carry text.
- **The landing state is part of the contract.** `#quiz-step-start` must carry BOTH
`.quiz-step` and `.active` in the server render -- a quiz that ships with no screen marked
active shows a visitor an empty box, and every other check here would still pass.
- **The interactive half, as the visitor's real journey.** `/tools/assets/ai-readiness-quiz.js`
binds `#quiz-start-btn` to `showStep(1)`, and delegated clicks on `.quiz-option` record the
answer and enable that step's `[data-action="next"]` button. The fence dispatches two REAL
clicks: Start must make `#quiz-step-1` the active step, and then answering question 1 must
enable Next.
- **Check order is load-bearing here and that is deliberate.** The evaluator drives all checks
against ONE shared page in declaration order, so `answering-a-question-enables-next` does
NOT re-click Start -- it continues from the state the previous check left, exactly as a
visitor would. Authoring it with its own Start click FAILED on first trial: the start button
is hidden once the quiz has advanced, and the click timed out at 30 s. Do not "fix" a later
step by making it self-contained; it cannot be.
mutants: 9/9 caught, every check watched red, baseline green
